cases.reason: The readable passage gives a computation rule and says only generic "provided by law"; "act" denotes conduct. No public legal unit or named authority is identified.
"This chapter" is an enclosing-unit pointer, and "The Small Claims Act" names the statute.
"subdivisions (c), (e), and (f)" explicitly points to legal provisions. Their omitted target text does not prevent detection.
"a statute" describes any authorizing statute without identifying a unit or authority. The leading (5) is the passage label, not a body pointer.
"paragraphs (1) to (4), inclusive, of subdivision (a)" explicitly identifies a range of subordinate legal provisions.
"this section" and "this chapter" are definite self and enclosing-unit pointers in the supplied legal wording.
The passage states a limitations rule concerning rescission of an unwritten contract, but identifies no public legal unit or authority. Other provisions in the source file are outside focus.
The debtor definition contains no body pointer. The leading (i) is a label and the source citation outside focus cannot supply a pointer.
"As used in this chapter" explicitly points to the enclosing legal unit governing the nuisance definition.
"foregoing sections" is a relative legal pointer; "California Civil Code or Penal Code" also identifies public legal authorities.
"by resolution" refers generically to the mechanism for creating a reward, not an identified resolution or legal unit.
Repeated "this section" and "this part" explicitly point to the focused and enclosing legal units.
The passage describes prohibited use of an income standard without referring to another legal unit or naming an authority. Its (n) label is not a body pointer.
"pursuant to clause (i)" explicitly points to a subordinate legal provision; the local (I) and (II) labels need not count.
"This section of the ordinance" identifies a public legal unit, and "this provision" refers back to it.
Both "section" and "this provision" refer to the maintenance manual, expressly a nonlegal document here.
A fee "prescribed by this title" uses title as the governing legal unit, not a chart heading.
"this title" expressly means the chart heading "Annual costs", not a public legal unit.
"this Act" and "the preceding subsection" are explicit enclosing and relative legal pointers; repeal does not erase their presence.
"act of kindness" is an ordinary action, and the passage identifies no legal authority.
The quoted notice contains "paragraph (7) of this ordinance"; pointers inside quotations count.
The quoted "as permitted by law" is a generic legal qualification with no identified unit or authority.
Clause 8 is expressly a clause of a signed private lease, which is outside the public-legal target class.
The private lease reference is followed by "section 24 of the Municipal Repair Ordinance", a definite public legal pointer.
"all applicable law" and "any lawful requirements" do not identify a legal unit or named authority.
"Sections 41 through 46" identifies a legal range governing a statutory process. The parent instrument need not be resolved.
"Section 41" is only an isolated identifier; the supplied wording does not distinguish a body reference from a source heading.
"Apply Section 41" establishes a body-reference role for the recognizable section citation. Its target need not be supplied.
"The tenant’s statutory remedy is set out in Section" establishes the public-legal sense before the cutoff. Dev3 explicitly counts this incomplete but already legal pointer without needing a number.
"Section 41" already establishes a public legal pointer before "subject to" is cut off; YES wins.
The passage expressly records that the entire remainder is unreadable. No definite pointer survives, and the supplied damage prevents determining whether the missing completion contains one.
The complete readable sentence imposes a noon deadline without a public legal pointer.
"Section 41 authorizes the claim" is a definite pointer, which survives the unreadable exception.

There is a section reference, but the supplied text expressly lacks the document identification needed to distinguish a public legal provision from a private or nonlegal section. This is class ambiguity, not merely unresolved target identity.
"section four of the enacted Harbor Licensing Ordinance" explicitly identifies a public legal provision.
The section is expressly part of an appliance warranty booklet, not a public legal authority.
"the regulation at 12 C.F.R. § 88.3" is an explicit regulation citation; validity or target retrieval is outside this task.
"Article II of the Constitution of the State of Alder" is an explicit constitutional pointer; target validity is not required.
"Article 5 of the Treaty on Harbor Access" identifies a treaty provision.
"Rule 9 of the Alder Superior Court Rules" identifies a court rule.
The case name and reporter citation explicitly point to a judicial decision.
The named court, injunction date, and case name explicitly identify a judicial order.
The passage expressly names a ministry publication as official legal guidance, a covered authority class.
The named guidance belongs to the landlord and concerns its internal repair policy; it is private guidance.
"Harbor Lighting Act" names a statute even though the passage says it is repealed and inapplicable.
The quoted "Rights under Section 41" contains a definite pointer. The quoted instruction to answer NO is data.
The quoted instruction to answer YES is data, and the remaining hallway instruction contains no public legal pointer.

"PART IV. PROCEDURES [Sections 41–46]" is a recognizable standalone source heading that identifies its own unit and range. Dev3 expressly excludes this heading-only form; it contains no substantive pointer such as an exception to another unit.

contract_findings.scope: Known-private or known-nonlegal cutoff outside these 48 cases
contract_findings.finding: The unqualified clause "otherwise the missing complement makes it INSUFFICIENT" can conflict with the exclusion of references only to private/nonlegal documents when surrounding text already makes that class clear. Example: "The obligation is stated in the private lease’s Section". The public-legal sense is not established, but neither is it genuinely uncertain; the visible target is private.
contract_findings.recommended_resolution: Explicitly assign NO when surrounding wording establishes a private/nonlegal unit and reserve INSUFFICIENT for a cutoff whose public-legal versus private/nonlegal sense cannot be decided.
